Student kills schoolmate and himself in livestreamed Philippine school attack, official says

A high school student carrying two pistols shot to death a fellow student before killing himself Tuesday in an attack in a southern Philippine high school campus that he livestreamed using a body-worn camera, police and other officials said. It was the second fatal school shooting in the country in just two months.

corpus.title: Zamboanga school shooter wasn't bullied or depressed, Angara says
corpus.signal_text:
Zamboanga school shooter wasn't bullied or depressed, Angara says
Content warning: Violence, school shooting, suicide
MANILA, Philippines — Education Secretary Sonny Angara denied two widely shared speculations about the Ateneo de Zamboanga shooting on Wednesday, August 19, saying there is no truth to reports that the student gunman was bullied or depressed.
"It's not true that the child is being bullied. It's also not true that he is depressed because he has a family network. He has many cousins," Angara told reporters today, after a closed-door briefing with Ateneo de Zamboanga University President Fr. Guillrey Anthony M. Andal, city officials and police.
The motive of the student gunman, Angara said, remains a "mystery." He cautioned the public to wait for confirmed details from the incident.
"It's better to not give conclusive remarks if the evidence is not yet clear," Angara said.
A Grade 8 student from Ateneo de Zamboanga opened fire on his schoolmates yesterday around 7:45 a.m. before turning the gun on himself and taking his own life.
The reported death toll includes two counts: the shooter himself and a Grade 10 student.
Angara said investigators cannot yet say whom the student specifically sought to target during the attack, which he had livestreamed on social media using a body-mounted camera.
The student allegedly entered two classrooms but fired a gun only in the second room.
"He didn't fire the gun in the first classroom he went to... So it's not really clear who the target is," Angara said.
Asked about reports that the shooter was a heavy gamer, Angara said: "Hindi rin natin alam kung totoo 'yon. Hindi pa conclusive 'yon. Maari, could be a factor but we don't know at this stage."
Angara, however, said the department is not ruling out possible influence on the student by online nihilistic violent groups.
The student brought two firearms to the attack, both owned by his father, a customs police officer at the Port of Zamboanga: one a Bureau of Customs-issued .40-caliber Glock 22 pistol and the other a personal licensed firearm.
How exactly the student got hold of a service firearm is not yet clear. Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla said today the father's claim that his son grabbed the two firearms from a gun bag left in a car was "highly improbable," given that trained officers know how to store weapons safely.
The father, Lt. Lars Jalani II, has since been placed under preventive suspension by the Bureau of Customs.

Restraint urged in reporting Zamboanga school shooting
MANILA, Philippines — The Presidential Communications Office (PCO) appealed to the media on Wednesday, August 19, to exercise restraint in reporting details about the school shooting incident in Zamboanga City.
The executive’s communications arm, through its Secretary Dave Gomez, stressed in a statement that state media were advised to exercise the “highest level of caution” in reporting tragedies involving minors.
It added that the office will not impose restrictions on private media entities but also called on them to report the incident responsibly.
“In particular, we ask for restraint in reporting that may compromise the dignity, safety, and privacy of minors, the bereaved families, and the ongoing response and investigation efforts, and to avoid details that may encourage copycat acts,” the statement read.
Limit info on alleged shooter
Meanwhile, psychiatrist Randy Dellosa told ANC earlier on Wednesday that the media should limit the information they present regarding the incident, especially about the alleged shooter.
“The less people talk about the perpetrator, the better,” Dellosa said.
The expert further explained that limiting information about the underage perpetrator will prevent the danger of him possibly being perceived as a “martyr” and idolized.
He also warned about copycat acts, which he said can be prevented by limiting information about the method or process of the incident.
“Potential perpetrators are studying the event… The less they know of the process, of what happened, the better,” Dellosa said.
He also said that reports must emphasize the victims, as incidents like these are not typical crimes but ones that leave trauma among the young people who witnessed them.
“The students themselves have experienced the impact of death. Teenage life is a time of invincibility eh…but now they’re afraid that the person beside them might be the one who might down them,” Dellosa said.
Day of mourning
Meanwhile, the local government unit of Zamboanga City earlier officially declared Wednesday a day of mourning for the two students who died in the incident.
Classes at all levels were suspended in both public and private schools within the city.
Ateneo de Zamboanga University, meanwhile, has issued a memorandum extending the suspension of classes until Thursday, August 20.

corpus.title: Philippine student killed in livestreamed school shooting
corpus.signal_text:
Audio By Vocalize
A student livestreamed himself shooting another schoolmate dead before taking his own life at a high school in the Philippines on Tuesday, authorities said.
The school shooting, the country's second in as many months, took place at Ateneo de Zamboanga University, a Catholic private institution in western Mindanao.
"What we know so far is that (the shooter) went to the classroom of our known victim. He shot the victim, and after doing that, he went up to the fifth floor and shot himself," regional police spokeswoman Shella Chang told AFP.
In a separate statement, interior secretary Victor Remulla confirmed the ninth-grade suspect had livestreamed the incident on social media. The alleged shooter's Facebook account has since been disabled.
In the video, which was circulated by local media, the barrel of a gun can be seen moving down a hallway in the style of a first-person shooter video game before being pointed into a classroom and fired.
Children in school uniforms are then seen screaming and rushing for an exit.
Police have not confirmed any additional injuries.
National police are now trying to "establish the motive behind the shooting, determine the ownership and source of the firearm used, and find out how it was brought inside the school campus", the interior ministry said in a statement.
Hours later, the Philippines' customs department issued a statement saying it had ordered the "preventative suspension" of an agent who owned the guns "allegedly used by the student involved".
Customs Deputy Chief of Staff Noel Bendijo told AFP they had acted on intelligence from their own officers in Zamboanga.
"The information is that he was the father of (the alleged shooter)... As for the actual firearms used and how the kid was able to access them, all of those are still under investigation," he said.
"We've also spoken with the party involved. He understands, but of course, he's also grieving because he also lost his child," Bendijo added.
"That's a nightmare for any parent."
Police said only that they were still investigating when asked about the customs report.
Ateneo de Zamboanga president Father Guillrey Andal, confirming the two fatalities, said the school was "deeply saddened" by the shooting and was cooperating with the investigation.
